title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (ADR bundle)
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It collects the primary decisions (ADRs), implementation guidelines, ownership, and migration steps so teams have a single reference when building production-grade services and model endpoints.

Goals
- Provide a consistent, low-friction developer experience across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Reduce operational toil and incident blast radius through clear defaults and minimum standards.
- Ensure performance and cost predictability via standardized SLOs, benchmarking, and rollout practices.

Scope
Applies to all services and teams owned by Engineering that:
- Expose HTTP/REST or gRPC APIs to internal or external consumers.
- Package and serve models through Redwood Serving Runtime or via officially supported model adapters.
- Manage infrastructure with company-managed or customer-managed (Private) deployments.

Principles
1) Consistency: same interface and observable signals across environments.
2) Secure by default: minimal exposed attack surface, encryption-at-rest & in-transit, least privilege.
3) Performance-aware: defaults and tooling should make common performance patterns easy.
4) Ownership & telemetry: every service has a single owner and emits standard telemetry.

1) API Standards
- API style: REST+JSON for public-facing simple services; gRPC for intra-service high-throughput RPC. Use OpenAPI v3 for REST schemas (required).
- Versioning: path-based major versioning: /v1/, /v2/. Backwards-compatible changes allowed within a major version.
- Error format: standard error envelope: {"error": {"code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "human message", "details": {...} }}. Map to HTTP semantics (4xx client errors, 5xx server errors).
- Status codes: use 200 for successful responses; 201 for resource creation; 202 for accepted async; 4xx/5xx per RFC semantics. Avoid 204 where a typed response is expected.
- Pagination & list semantics: cursor-based pagination preferred (cursor, limit). Include total_count only where it is cheap to compute.
- Authentication: all public-facing endpoints must support token-based auth (JWT or API key). Use mutual TLS for sensitive customer Private endpoints.
- Rate limiting & quotas: services must expose rate limit headers and honor client tiers; default per-service rate limit configured in the API gateway.
- OpenAPI & contract testing: every public API must publish an OpenAPI file to the central registry and include an automated contract test as part of CI.

2) Coding Standards
- Languages & runtimes: preferred languages are Go (services) and Python (ML tooling). Use TypeScript for front-end/admin tooling. Exceptions require sign-off.
- Linting & formatting: Enforce gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, black/flake8/ruff for Python, eslint/prettier for TypeScript. CI must fail on lint errors.
- Testing: unit tests target >=70% coverage for new modules; critical path components require >85%. Include deterministic integration tests in CI (containerized).
- Reviews & PR process: require at least one reviewer from the owning team and one cross-team reviewer for public-facing changes. Document intended behavior in PR description and link to design.
- Dependency policy: prefer minimal transitive dependencies. Security team must review dependencies flagged by SCA tooling with CVSS >=7.

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC & deployment)
- IaC: Terraform for cloud resources (main repo: infra/terraform) with modules for common constructs (networking, kms, monitoring). Policy-as-code (Sentinel/OPA) enforced in CI.
- Environments: dev/staging/production parity required. No manual changes in production; all changes via IaC and CI/CD.
- Network: services must run in private subnets with NAT egress; customer Private deployments optionally allow customer-managed networking but must meet minimum CIDR & firewall rules.
- Secrets: use KMS-backed secrets stores (HashiCorp Vault or cloud secret manager). No plaintext secrets in repos.
- Capacity and scaling: autoscaling policies and safe default limits provided by platform. Teams must provide load-testing runbooks for capacity planning.

4) Model-Serving Standards
- Model packaging: models must include a manifest (model_manifest.json) listing architecture, tokenizer, precision/quantization, and required runtime.
- Versioning & artifacts: immutable model artifacts stored in dedicated artifact stores with semantic version tags and checksum metadata.
- Quantization & profiles: quantization profiles must be recorded (e.g., int8, 4-bit) with quality regression test results. See quantization-profiles guideline.
- Rollouts & compatibility: canary + gradual rollout recommended for model changes. Rollouts must define rollback criteria (latency, error rate, quality regression threshold).
- KV cache & warmup: models with large KV caches must expose warming endpoints and prefetch tooling. Default cold-start budget = 200ms for critical production endpoints.
- Fallbacks: multi-tier model routing: prefer primary model; fallback to compatible variant on overload or degraded quality. Routing policies configured at the control plane.

5) Observability Standards
- Metrics: emit prometheus-style metrics. Required service metrics: request_count, request_duration_seconds (histogram with p50/p95/p99), error_count, model_inference_latency_seconds, cache_hit_ratio.
- Tracing: instrument critical paths with OpenTelemetry. Traces must include request id, model id, shard id, and route decision metadata.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with severity, timestamp (UTC), request_id, user_id (when available), route, and error details. Sensitive data must be redacted before logging.
- Dashboards & alerts: standard dashboards per service (overview, latency, errors, capacity). Alerting thresholds aligned with SLOs; use PagerDuty for production-critical pages.
- SLO & Error budgeting: standard SLO template: Availability (p99 successful response) and Latency (p95 below configured threshold). See Performance Standards below for default targets.

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarking
- SLOs (default for public model endpoints):
  - Latency: p95 <= 300ms for simple text generation endpoints (small-context), p95 <= 800ms for large-context or multimodal endpoints.
  - Availability: 99.9% (monthly) for hosted and dedicated plans; 99.5% for Private deployments (contracted SLA).
  - Throughput: per-instance throughput documented in model profile; teams must publish per-device tokens/sec at 1, 8, and 32 concurrent requests.
- Benchmarking: every model/service must include a benchmark report with representative prompts, tokenization settings, batch sizes, and hardware matrix. Benchmarks stored in benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
- Load testing: run load tests for major releases and capacity changes. Define acceptance criteria (no >2x baseline error rate, p95 latency increase <20%).
- Cost/perf tradeoffs: quantization and batching recommendations must be accompanied by quality regression metrics and cost-per-token estimates.

7) ADRs (Decision Records)
- ADR process: major architectural decisions must be recorded as ADRs (title, status, context, decision, consequences, date, owners). Store ADRs under arch-docs/adr-YYYY-MM-DD.md and register in Confluence index.
- Summary of key existing ADRs relevant to this bundle: 
  - ADR-2025-02: Adopt OpenAPI v3 for REST contracts and require contract tests.
  - ADR-2025-07: Use Go for core serving control plane services (performance & binary portability).
  - ADR-2025-09: Model artifact immutability and artifact-store requirement.
  - ADR-2025-11: Standardize metrics and tracing fields for model inference telemetry.

8) Ownership & Governance
- Ownership: each service and model endpoint must have a documented owner (team + primary contact) in the service registry. Platform team owns runtime, rollout tooling, and global policy enforcement.
- Reviews: architecture changes that touch two or more teams require a technical design review meeting and ADR within 2 weeks of approval.
- Exceptions: request exceptions via the architecture exceptions process (submit RFC, include risk & mitigation). Exceptions expire after 6 months unless renewed.

9) Migration & Rollout Plan (for services that do not currently conform)
1. Inventory: run the conformance scanner to identify gaps (OpenAPI, metrics, SLOs, IaC).
2. Prioritize gaps by risk and customer exposure.
3. Implement fixes in staging with CI gating.
4. Run performance & regression tests; document results.
5. Canary rollout with observability guardrails then full rollout.

10) Acceptance Criteria & CI Checks (must be part of PR)
- OpenAPI file present and validated.
- Linting and unit tests pass.
- Metrics & traces instrumented (smoke test emits metrics).
- Benchmark report included for model endpoints.
- IaC diffs validated by policy-as-code.

Appendix: Example OpenAPI snippet (required for REST services)
---
paths:
  /v1/generate:
    post:
      summary: Generate text from model
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful generation
        '4XX':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ErrorResponse'

---
